Ice age.fact: The term is applied in several different senses to very long and comparatively short periods of cooling.  Colder periods are called glacials or ice ages, and warmer periods are called interglacials.  Earth's climate alternates between icehouse and greenhouse periods based on whether there are glaciers on the planet, and for most of Earth's history it has been in a greenhouse period with little or no permanent ice.  Over the very long term, Earth is currently in an icehouse period called the Late Cenozoic Ice Age, which started 34 million years ago.  There have been colder and warmer periods within this ice age, and the term is also applied to the Quaternary glaciation, which started 2.  Within this period, the Last Interglacial ended 115,000 years ago, and was followed by the Last Glacial Period (LGP), which gave way to the current warm Holocene, which started 11,700 years ago.  The most severe cold period of the LGP was the Last Glacial Maximum, which reached its maximum between 26,000 and 20,000 years ago

In a paper published in 1824, Esmark proposed changes in climate as the cause of those glaciations.  He attempted to show that they originated from changes in Earth's orbit.  Esmark discovered the similarity between moraines near Haukalivatnet lake near sea level in Rogaland and moraines at branches of Jostedalsbreen. Ice age.question: They mainly drew upon the preceding works of Venetz, _____ and on their own fieldwork
Ice age.fact: Schimper spent the summer months of 1836 at Devens, near Bex, in the Swiss Alps with his former university friend Louis Agassiz (1801–1873) and Jean de Charpentier.  Schimper, Charpentier and possibly Venetz convinced Agassiz that there had been a time of glaciation.  During the winter of 1836–37, Agassiz and Schimper developed the theory of a sequence of glaciations.  They mainly drew upon the preceding works of Venetz, Charpentier and on their own fieldwork.  Agassiz appears to have been already familiar with Bernhardi's paper at that time.  At the beginning of 1837, Schimper coined the term "ice age" ("Eiszeit") for the period of the glaciers.  In July 1837 Agassiz presented their synthesis before the annual meeting of the Swiss Society for Natural Research at Neuchâtel

Ice age.subject: World Geography
Ice age.question: In order to persuade the skeptics, _____ embarked on geological fieldwork
Ice age.fact: In July 1837 Agassiz presented their synthesis before the annual meeting of the Swiss Society for Natural Research at Neuchâtel.  The audience was very critical, and some were opposed to the new theory because it contradicted the established opinions on climatic history.  Most contemporary scientists thought that Earth had been gradually cooling down since its birth as a molten globe.  In order to persuade the skeptics, Agassiz embarked on geological fieldwork.  He published his book Study on Glaciers ("Études sur les glaciers") in 1840.  Charpentier was put out by this, as he had also been preparing a book about the glaciation of the Alps.  Charpentier felt that Agassiz should have given him precedence as it was he who had introduced Agassiz to in-depth glacial research

Iceland.fact: While early settlers cultivated barley, the cooling climate from the 12th century onwards made grain cultivation increasingly difficult.  The Little Ice Age began around 1300 bringing colder and more unpredictable weather, further shortening growing seasons and making farming more challenging.  The Black Death reached Iceland in 1402–1404 and again in 1494–1495, with devastating effects.  The first outbreak is estimated to have killed 50–60% of the population, while the second resulted in a 30–50% mortality rate.  These pandemics significantly reduced the population, leading to social and economic disruptions.  In 1380, after the death of Haakon VI, his son Olaf II of Denmark succeeded to the Norwegian throne, uniting the crowns of Denmark and Norway under one monarch. Indrasan.fact: Mount Indrasan is located at an altitude of 6221 metres above sea level in Kullu district, Himachal Pradesh.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: The _____ was King of Wessex from 689 to 726.
Ine of Wessex.fact: Ine or Ini (died in or after 726) was King of Wessex from 689 to 726. At Ine's accession, his kingdom dominated much of what is now southern England.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Ine or Ini (died in or after 726) was _____ of Wessex from 689 to 726
Ine of Wessex.fact: Ine or Ini (died in or after 726) was King of Wessex from 689 to 726. At Ine's accession, his kingdom dominated much of what is now southern England.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: However, he was unable to retain the territorial gains of his predecessor, Cædwalla of Wessex, who had expanded _____ territory substantially
Ine of Wessex.fact: However, he was unable to retain the territorial gains of his predecessor, Cædwalla of Wessex, who had expanded West Saxon territory substantially. By the end of Ine's reign, the kingdoms of Kent, Sussex, and Essex were no longer under West Saxon sway; however, Ine maintained control of what is now Hampshire, and consolidated and extended Wessex's territory in the western peninsula.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Ine is noted for his code of laws (_____ asetnessa or "laws of Ine"), which he issued in about 694
Ine of Wessex.fact: Ine is noted for his code of laws (Ines asetnessa or "laws of Ine"), which he issued in about 694.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: These laws were the first issued by an _____-Saxon king outside Kent
Ine of Wessex.fact: These laws were the first issued by an Anglo-Saxon king outside Kent. They shed much light on the history of Anglo-Saxon society, and reveal Ine's Christian convictions.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: They shed much light on the history of Anglo-Saxon society, and reveal Ine's _____ convictions
Ine of Wessex.fact: They shed much light on the history of Anglo-Saxon society, and reveal Ine's Christian convictions.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Trade increased significantly during Ine's reign, with the town of Hamwic (now _____) becoming prominent
Ine of Wessex.fact: Trade increased significantly during Ine's reign, with the town of Hamwic (now Southampton) becoming prominent.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: It was probably during Ine's reign that the _____ began to mint coins, though none have been found that bear his name
Ine of Wessex.fact: It was probably during Ine's reign that the West Saxons began to mint coins, though none have been found that bear his name.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Ine abdicated in 726 to go to _____, leaving, in the words of the contemporary chronicler Bede, the kingdom to "younger men"
Ine of Wessex.fact: Ine abdicated in 726 to go to Rome, leaving, in the words of the contemporary chronicler Bede, the kingdom to "younger men".

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Ine was born around 670 and his siblings included a brother, Ingild, and two sisters, _____ and Cwenburg
Ine of Wessex.fact: Ine was born around 670 and his siblings included a brother, Ingild, and two sisters, Cuthburh and Cwenburg. Cuthburh was married to King Aldfrith of Northumbria, and Ine himself was married to Æthelburg.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Ingild is given by the Anglo-Saxon royal genealogies as ancestor of king Egbert of Wessex and the subsequent kings of _____
Ine of Wessex.fact: Ingild is given by the Anglo-Saxon royal genealogies as ancestor of king Egbert of Wessex and the subsequent kings of England.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Cuthburh was married to _____ of Northumbria, and Ine himself was married to Æthelburg
Ine of Wessex.fact: Cuthburh was married to King Aldfrith of Northumbria, and Ine himself was married to Æthelburg.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Bede tells that Ine was "of the blood royal", by which he means the royal line of the Gewisse, the early _____ tribal name
Ine of Wessex.fact: Bede tells that Ine was "of the blood royal", by which he means the royal line of the Gewisse, the early West Saxon tribal name. The genealogy of Ine is known from the Anglian King-list, the West Saxon Genealogical Regnal List (which may share a common source with the Anglian King-list) and the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle (which certainly drew on and adapted an early version of the West Saxon Genealogical Regnal List, alongside other sources).

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Cædwalla abdicated in 688 and departed for _____ to be baptized
Ine of Wessex.fact: Cædwalla abdicated in 688 and departed for Rome to be baptized.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: According to the _____, Ine reigned for 37 years, abdicating in 726
Ine of Wessex.fact: According to the West Saxon Genealogical Regnal List, Ine reigned for 37 years, abdicating in 726.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Ine acknowledges his father's help in his code of laws, and there is also a surviving land-grant that indicates _____ was still reigning in Wessex after Ine's accession
Ine of Wessex.fact: Ine may have ruled alongside his father, Cenred, for a period: there is weak evidence for joint kingships, and stronger evidence of subkings reigning under a dominant ruler in Wessex, not long before this time. Ine acknowledges his father's help in his code of laws, and there is also a surviving land-grant that indicates Cenred was still reigning in Wessex after Ine's accession.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: The upper _____ valley on both sides of the river had long been the territory of the Gewisse, though Cædwalla had lost territory north of the river to the kingdom of Mercia before Ine's accession
Ine of Wessex.fact: The upper Thames valley on both sides of the river had long been the territory of the Gewisse, though Cædwalla had lost territory north of the river to the kingdom of Mercia before Ine's accession.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: To the west, _____ of Wessex is known to have reached the Bristol Channel one hundred years before
Ine of Wessex.fact: To the west, Ceawlin of Wessex is known to have reached the Bristol Channel one hundred years before.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: On the _____' eastern border was the kingdom of the East Saxons, which included London and what is now Surrey
Ine of Wessex.fact: The West Saxons had since expanded further down the southwestern peninsula, pushing back the boundary with the British kingdom of Dumnonia, which was probably roughly equivalent to modern Devon and Cornwall. On the West Saxons' eastern border was the kingdom of the East Saxons, which included London and what is now Surrey.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: To the southeast were the _____, on the coast east of the Isle of Wight
Ine of Wessex.fact: To the southeast were the South Saxons, on the coast east of the Isle of Wight.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Beyond Sussex lay the kingdom of _____
Ine of Wessex.fact: Beyond Sussex lay the kingdom of Kent. Ine retained control of the Isle of Wight, and made further advances in Dumnonia, but the territorial gains Cædwalla had made in Sussex, Surrey and Kent were all lost by the end of Ine's reign.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Ine's predecessor, Cædwalla, had made himself overlord of most of these southern kingdoms, though he had not been able to prevent _____ inroads along the upper Thames
Ine of Wessex.fact: Ine's predecessor, Cædwalla, had made himself overlord of most of these southern kingdoms, though he had not been able to prevent Mercian inroads along the upper Thames.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Ine retained control of the Isle of Wight, and made further advances in _____, but the territorial gains Cædwalla had made in Sussex, Surrey and Kent were all lost by the end of Ine's reign
Ine of Wessex.fact: Ine retained control of the Isle of Wight, and made further advances in Dumnonia, but the territorial gains Cædwalla had made in Sussex, Surrey and Kent were all lost by the end of Ine's reign.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: The value of the amount offered to Ine by _____ is uncertain; most manuscripts of the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle record "thirty thousand", and some specify thirty thousand pounds
Ine of Wessex.fact: The value of the amount offered to Ine by Wihtred is uncertain; most manuscripts of the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle record "thirty thousand", and some specify thirty thousand pounds.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Ine kept the _____, who had been conquered by Cædwalla in 686, in subjugation for a period
Ine of Wessex.fact: Ine kept the South Saxons, who had been conquered by Cædwalla in 686, in subjugation for a period.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: King Nothhelm of _____ is referred to in a charter of 692 as a kinsman of Ine (perhaps by marriage)
Ine of Wessex.fact: King Nothhelm of Sussex is referred to in a charter of 692 as a kinsman of Ine (perhaps by marriage). Sussex was still under West Saxon domination in 710, when Nothhelm is recorded as having campaigned with Ine in the west against Dumnonia.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Sussex was still under _____ domination in 710, when Nothhelm is recorded as having campaigned with Ine in the west against Dumnonia
Ine of Wessex.fact: Sussex was still under West Saxon domination in 710, when Nothhelm is recorded as having campaigned with Ine in the west against Dumnonia.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Control of _____, which may never have been an independent kingdom, passed between Kent, Mercia, Essex, and Wessex in the years before Ine's reign
Ine of Wessex.fact: Control of Surrey, which may never have been an independent kingdom, passed between Kent, Mercia, Essex, and Wessex in the years before Ine's reign. Essex also included London, and the diocese of London included Surrey; this appears to have been a source of friction between Ine and the East Saxon and Mercian kings until the province was transferred to the diocese of Winchester in 705.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Evidence for Ine's early control of _____ comes from the introduction to his laws, in which he refers to Eorcenwald, bishop of London, as "my bishop"
Ine of Wessex.fact: Control of Surrey, which may never have been an independent kingdom, passed between Kent, Mercia, Essex, and Wessex in the years before Ine's reign. Essex also included London, and the diocese of London included Surrey; this appears to have been a source of friction between Ine and the East Saxon and Mercian kings until the province was transferred to the diocese of Winchester in 705.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Ine's subsequent relations with the _____ are illuminated by a letter written in 704 or 705 by Bishop Wealdhere of London to Brihtwold, the Archbishop of Canterbury
Ine of Wessex.fact: Ine's subsequent relations with the East Saxons are illuminated by a letter written in 704 or 705 by Bishop Wealdhere of London to Brihtwold, the Archbishop of Canterbury. The rulers that Wealdhere refers to are Sigeheard and Swæfred of the East Saxons, and the cause of the discord was the East Saxons' sheltering of exiles from the West Saxons.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: The rulers that _____ refers to are Sigeheard and Swæfred of the East Saxons, and the cause of the discord was the East Saxons' sheltering of exiles from the West Saxons
Ine of Wessex.fact: Ine's subsequent relations with the East Saxons are illuminated by a letter written in 704 or 705 by Bishop Wealdhere of London to Brihtwold, the Archbishop of Canterbury. The rulers that Wealdhere refers to are Sigeheard and Swæfred of the East Saxons, and the cause of the discord was the East Saxons' sheltering of exiles from the West Saxons.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: The letter refers to "disputes and discords" that had arisen "between the king of the _____ and the rulers of our country"
Ine of Wessex.fact: The letter refers to "disputes and discords" that had arisen "between the king of the West Saxons and the rulers of our country". The rulers that Wealdhere refers to are Sigeheard and Swæfred of the East Saxons, and the cause of the discord was the East Saxons' sheltering of exiles from the West Saxons.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: A council at _____ was planned to resolve the disputes
Ine of Wessex.fact: A council at Brentford was planned to resolve the disputes.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: By this point _____ had clearly passed out of West Saxon control
Ine of Wessex.fact: By this point Surrey had clearly passed out of West Saxon control. Bede records that Ine held Sussex in subjection for "several years", but in 722 an exile named Ealdbert fled to Surrey and Sussex, and Ine invaded Sussex as a result.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Bede records that Ine held _____ in subjection for "several years", but in 722 an exile named Ealdbert fled to Surrey and Sussex, and Ine invaded Sussex as a result
Ine of Wessex.fact: Bede records that Ine held Sussex in subjection for "several years", but in 722 an exile named Ealdbert fled to Surrey and Sussex, and Ine invaded Sussex as a result. Sussex had evidently broken away from West Saxon domination some time before this.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Three years later Ine invaded again, this time killing _____
Ine of Wessex.fact: Three years later Ine invaded again, this time killing Ealdberht. It has been suggested that Ealdberht was a son of Ine, or a son of Ine's brother Ingild.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: It has been suggested that _____ was a son of Ine, or a son of Ine's brother Ingild
Ine of Wessex.fact: Three years later Ine invaded again, this time killing Ealdberht. It has been suggested that Ealdberht was a son of Ine, or a son of Ine's brother Ingild.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Sussex had evidently broken away from _____ domination some time before this
Ine of Wessex.fact: By this point Surrey had clearly passed out of West Saxon control. Sussex had evidently broken away from West Saxon domination some time before this.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: It has traditionally been thought that Ine's advance brought him control of what is now Devon, the new border with _____ being the river Tamar
Ine of Wessex.fact: It has traditionally been thought that Ine's advance brought him control of what is now Devon, the new border with Dumnonia being the river Tamar.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: However, this does not match with subsequent events such as the Battle of Hehil or _____ driving the Britons from Isca (Exeter)
Ine of Wessex.fact: However, this does not match with subsequent events such as the Battle of Hehil or Athelstan driving the Britons from Isca (Exeter).

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: The Annales Cambriae, a tenth-century chronicle, records that in 722 the _____ defeated their enemies at the Battle of Hehil
Ine of Wessex.fact: The Annales Cambriae, a tenth-century chronicle, records that in 722 the British defeated their enemies at the Battle of Hehil.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: The "enemies" must be Ine or his people, but the location is unidentified; historians have suggested locations in both _____ and Devon
Ine of Wessex.fact: The "enemies" must be Ine or his people, but the location is unidentified; historians have suggested locations in both Cornwall and Devon.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Ine fought a battle at Woden's Barrow in _____ in 715, either against the Mercians under Ceolred or together with them against an unnamed opponent; the result is not recorded
Ine of Wessex.fact: Ine fought a battle at Woden's Barrow in Wiltshire in 715, either against the Mercians under Ceolred or together with them against an unnamed opponent; the result is not recorded. Woden's Barrow is a tumulus, now called Adam's Grave, at Alton Prior, Wiltshire.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Woden's _____ is a tumulus, now called Adam's Grave, at Alton Prior, Wiltshire
Ine of Wessex.fact: Ine fought a battle at Woden's Barrow in Wiltshire in 715, either against the Mercians under Ceolred or together with them against an unnamed opponent; the result is not recorded. Woden's Barrow is a tumulus, now called Adam's Grave, at Alton Prior, Wiltshire.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: A quarrel apparently arose in the royal family soon afterwards: in 722, according to the _____, Ine's queen Æthelburg destroyed Taunton, which her husband had built earlier in his reign, around 710
Ine of Wessex.fact: A quarrel apparently arose in the royal family soon afterwards: in 722, according to the Chronicle, Ine's queen Æthelburg destroyed Taunton, which her husband had built earlier in his reign, around 710.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: By about 710, in the middle of Ine's reign, the trading settlement of _____ had become established on the west bank of the river Itchen; the site is now part of the modern city of Southampton
Ine of Wessex.fact: By about 710, in the middle of Ine's reign, the trading settlement of Hamwic had become set up on the west bank of the river Itchen; the site is now part of the modern city of Southampton.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Further evidence of trade comes from finds of imported goods such as quernstones, whetstones, and pottery; and finds of sceattas from the town include _____ coins
Ine of Wessex.fact: Further evidence of trade comes from finds of imported goods such as quernstones, whetstones, and pottery; and finds of sceattas from the town include Frisian coins.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: It is not known whether Ine took an interest in _____, but some of the goods he favoured, including luxuries, were imported there, and the merchants would probably have needed royal protection
Ine of Wessex.fact: It is not known whether Ine took an interest in Hamwic, but some of the goods he favoured, including luxuries, were imported there, and the merchants would probably have needed royal protection. The total population of Hamwic has been estimated at 5,000, and this high population itself implies Ine's involvement, since no-one but the king would have been able to arrange to feed and house such a large group of people.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: The growth of trade after about 700 was paralleled by an expansion of the area of circulation of the sceat, the common coin of the day, to include the upper _____ valley
Ine of Wessex.fact: The growth of trade after about 700 was paralleled by an expansion of the area of circulation of the sceat, the common coin of the day, to include the upper Thames valley.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: It is thought that the first _____ coinage was minted during Ine's reign, though no coins bearing his name have been found—sceattas typically gave no hint of the reigning king
Ine of Wessex.fact: It is thought that the first West Saxon coinage was minted during Ine's reign, though no coins bearing his name have been found—sceattas typically gave no hint of the reigning king.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: In the 670s or 680s, a code was issued in the names of _____ and Eadric of Kent
Ine of Wessex.fact: In the 670s or 680s, a code was issued in the names of Hlothhere and Eadric of Kent.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: The next kings to issue laws were _____ of Kent and Ine
Ine of Wessex.fact: The next kings to issue laws were Wihtred of Kent and Ine. The dates of Wihtred's and Ine's laws are somewhat uncertain, but there is reason to believe that Wihtred's laws were issued on 6 September 695, while Ine's laws were written in 694 or shortly before.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: The dates of _____'s and Ine's laws are somewhat uncertain, but there is reason to believe that Wihtred's laws were issued on 6 September 695, while Ine's laws were written in 694 or shortly before
Ine of Wessex.fact: The next kings to issue laws were Wihtred of Kent and Ine. The dates of Wihtred's and Ine's laws are somewhat uncertain, but there is reason to believe that Wihtred's laws were issued on 6 September 695, while Ine's laws were written in 694 or shortly before.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Ine had recently agreed to peaceful terms with _____ over compensation for the death of Mul, and there are indications that the two rulers collaborated to some degree in producing their laws
Ine of Wessex.fact: The next kings to issue laws were Wihtred of Kent and Ine. The dates of Wihtred's and Ine's laws are somewhat uncertain, but there is reason to believe that Wihtred's laws were issued on 6 September 695, while Ine's laws were written in 694 or shortly before.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Another sign of collaboration is that Wihtred's laws use gesith, a _____ term for noble, in place of the Kentish term eorlcund
Ine of Wessex.fact: Another sign of collaboration is that Wihtred's laws use gesith, a West Saxon term for noble, in place of the Kentish term eorlcund.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: It is possible that Ine and _____ issued the law codes as an act of prestige, to re-establish authority after periods of disruption in both kingdoms
Ine of Wessex.fact: Ine had recently agreed to peaceful terms with Wihtred over compensation for the death of Mul, and there are indications that the two rulers collaborated to some degree in producing their laws. Another sign of collaboration is that Wihtred's laws use gesith, a West Saxon term for noble, in place of the Kentish term eorlcund.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Ine's laws survive only because _____ the Great appended them to his own code of laws
Ine of Wessex.fact: Ine's laws survive only because Alfred the Great appended them to his own code of laws. The oldest surviving manuscript, and only complete copy, is in Corpus Christi College, Cambridge MS 173, which contains both Alfred's and Ine's law codes and the oldest extant text of the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: The oldest surviving manuscript, and only complete copy, is in Corpus Christi College, Cambridge MS _____, which contains both Alfred's and Ine's law codes and the oldest extant text of the Anglo-Saxo
Ine of Wessex.fact: The oldest surviving manuscript, and only complete copy, is in Corpus Christi College, Cambridge MS 173, which contains both Alfred's and Ine's law codes and the oldest extant text of the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle. One was originally a complete copy of Ine's laws, part of British Library MS Cotton Otho B xi, but that manuscript was largely destroyed in 1731 by a fire at Ashburnham House in which only Chapters 66 to 76.2 of Ine's laws escaped destruction.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: A fragment of Ine's laws can also be found in _____ 277
Ine of Wessex.fact: A fragment of Ine's laws can also be found in British Library Burney MS 277.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Ingrid Ivarsen suggests that the laws were originally composed in Latin and translated into _____
Ine of Wessex.fact: Ingrid Ivarsen suggests that the laws were originally composed in Latin and translated into Old English.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Three people are named: bishops _____ and Hædde, and Ine's father, King Cenred
Ine of Wessex.fact: Three people are named: bishops Eorcenwald and Hædde, and Ine's father, King Cenred.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Ine was a _____ king, whose intent to encourage Christianity is clear from the laws
Ine of Wessex.fact: Ine was a Christian king, whose intent to encourage Christianity is clear from the laws. The oath of a communicant, for example, is declared to carry more weight than that of a non-Christian, and baptism and religious observance are also addressed.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: The oath of a communicant, for example, is declared to carry more weight than that of a non-_____, and baptism and religious observance are also addressed
Ine of Wessex.fact: Ine was a Christian king, whose intent to encourage Christianity is clear from the laws. The oath of a communicant, for example, is declared to carry more weight than that of a non-Christian, and baptism and religious observance are also addressed.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Significant attention is also paid to civil issues—more than in the contemporary _____ laws
Ine of Wessex.fact: Significant attention is also paid to civil issues—more than in the contemporary Kentish laws.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: One of the laws states that common land might be enclosed by several ceorls (the contemporary name for _____ freemen)
Ine of Wessex.fact: One of the laws states that common land might be enclosed by several ceorls (the contemporary name for Saxon freemen).

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Not all of Wessex used this system, however: it was not used in _____, for example
Ine of Wessex.fact: Not all of Wessex used this system, however: it was not used in Devon, for example.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: It is notable that, although issued by the Saxon king of a Saxon kingdom, the term used in the laws to define Ine's _____ subjects is Englisc
Ine of Wessex.fact: The evidence they provide for the incomplete integration of the two populations is supported by research into placename history, the history of religious houses, and local archaeology, which indicates that the western part of Wessex was thinly settled by the Germanic newcomers at the time the laws were issued. It is notable that, although issued by the Saxon king of a Saxon kingdom, the term used in the laws to define Ine's Germanic subjects is Englisc.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: This reflects the existence, even at this early date, of a common _____ identity encompassing all the Germanic peoples of Britain
Ine of Wessex.fact: The laws made separate provision for Ine's English and British subjects, favouring the former over the latter; the weregilds paid for Britons were half of those paid for Saxons of the same social class, and their oaths also counted for less. This reflects the existence, even at this early date, of a common English identity encompassing all the Germanic peoples of Britain.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: The laws themselves demonstrate Ine's _____ convictions, specifying fines for failing to baptize infants or to tithe
Ine of Wessex.fact: The laws themselves demonstrate Ine's Christian convictions, specifying fines for failing to baptize infants or to tithe.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Ine supported the church by patronising religious houses, especially in the new diocese of _____, which had been divided from the diocese of Winchester in 705
Ine of Wessex.fact: Ine supported the church by patronising religious houses, especially in the new diocese of Sherborne, which had been divided from the diocese of Winchester in 705.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: Ine had opposed this division, ignoring threats of excommunication from _____, but he agreed to it when Bishop Haedde died
Ine of Wessex.fact: Ine had opposed this division, ignoring threats of excommunication from Canterbury, but he agreed to it when Bishop Haedde died.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: At the bishop _____'s suggestion in 705, Ine built the church which later became Wells Cathedral, and the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle also records that Ine built a minster at Glastonbury
Ine of Wessex.fact: At the bishop Aldhelm's suggestion in 705, Ine built the church which later became Wells Cathedral, and the Anglo-Saxon Chronicle also records that Ine built a minster at Glastonbury.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: This must refer to additional building or re-building since there was already a _____ monastery at Glastonbury
Ine of Wessex.fact: This must refer to additional building or re-building since there was already a British monastery at Glastonbury.

Ine of Wessex.subject: World Geography
Ine of Wessex.question: He is also connected with the oldest known _____ synods, presiding at one himself and apparently addressing the assembled clerics
Ine of Wessex.fact: He is also connected with the oldest known West Saxon synods, presiding at one himself and apparently addressing the assembled clerics.
